title: Doubled pawns in context

D0.outcome: Explains that doubled pawns are weak mainly when they advance and have value when they stay still, and that the verdict depends on the whole position.

D1.outcome: Lists, for a given doubled-pawn structure, what compensates (bishop pair, open file, central control) and what is lost.

D2.outcome: In unlabeled positions, decides whether to create or avoid doubled pawns, and how to provoke the owner into advancing them.

D3.outcome: Predicts how one feature (the bishop pair, an open file, the phase) flips the verdict.

misconceptions: Doubled pawns count as one pawn.
conditions: To exploit doubled pawns, first induce the owner to advance them; their real strength is that they hold out when they stay still.
They are weak when isolated or stuck with no way to create a passer.
contrasts: The doubled pawns give the bishop pair, an open file or central control.
'doubled pawns are a chimera in the early game' (too strong).
Doubled pawns far from any play.
